section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: Ministry officials said Bangladesh would propose at the joint technical committee that all legal agencies be allowed to send workers, and that since the MoU ran to December there was no scope for a new agreement, only for amending the existing one [MP0536, MP0537, MP0538].
new_str: Ministry officials said Bangladesh would propose at the joint technical committee that all legal agencies be allowed to send workers, and that since the MoU ran to December 2025 there was no scope for a new agreement, only for amending the existing one [MP0536, MP0537, MP0538].
problem: The source (Prothom Alo, 15 May 2025) says the MoU ran to 'আগামী ডিসেম্বর', i.e. December 2025; bare 'December' reads as the 31 December 2026 expiry given elsewhere, hiding a third conflicting expiry date.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: > - Does the 2022 MoU expire on 31 December 2026 [Z0156] or did it expire in August 2026 [MP0492], and under which terms are the 2026 workers going?
new_str: > - Was the MoU signed on 19 December 2021 [W0027] or 18 December 2022 [MP0438], and does it expire on 31 December 2026 [Z0156], or did it expire in December 2025 [MP0538] or August 2026 [MP0492]? Under which terms are the 2026 workers going?
problem: Need to know omits the third expiry date reported (December 2025, MP0538) and the conflict over the signing date: BMET's office order (W0027) dates the MoU to 19 December 2021, and the guide elsewhere calls it the 2021 MoU, while the Ministry's 2026 releases (MP0438, Z0156) say 18 December 2022.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: - **1 December 2024:** former ambassador M Humayun Kabir, president of the Bangladesh Enterprise Institute, said in an interview that the market had closed and had reopened on the initiative of the Chief Adviser, Muhammad Yunus [MP0253, MP0254, MP0197].
new_str: - **1 December 2024:** former ambassador M Humayun Kabir, president of the Bangladesh Enterprise Institute, said in an interview that the market had closed and had reopened on the initiative of the Chief Adviser, Muhammad Yunus [MP0253, MP0254].
problem: MP0197 is about something else (Anwar Ibrahim's 4 October 2024 press conference on 18,000 workers), not Humayun Kabir's interview.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: - **August 2025:** the Chief Adviser was to visit Malaysia for three days from 11 August and meet Anwar Ibrahim in Putrajaya on 12 August; a senior foreign ministry official said removing Bangladeshis' problems in Malaysia's labour market and taking more workers would get priority, alongside five MoUs on other subjects [MP0606, MP0607, MP0608].
new_str: - **August 2025:** the Chief Adviser was to visit Malaysia for three days from 11 August and meet Anwar Ibrahim in Putrajaya on 12 August; a senior foreign ministry official said removing Bangladeshis' problems in Malaysia's labour market and taking more workers would get priority; five MoUs on other subjects might be signed [MP0606, MP0607, MP0608].
problem: The source says the five MoUs 'might be' signed; the sentence states them as part of the agenda and ties them to the official's statement.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: Ministers announced or forecast a reopening several times from 2025 before the restart of 15 October 2026
new_str: Ministers and government advisers announced or forecast a reopening several times from 2024 before the restart of 15 October 2026
problem: Lead sentence not true of the cases cited/listed: MP0412 is Mahdi Amin, the Prime Minister's adviser, and MP0630 an interim-government adviser, not ministers; and the list's first forecasts (MP0205, MP0253, MP0260) are from 2024.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: - 2024: fewer than one lakh went after the market closed, a fall of more than two lakh (BMET data, Prothom Alo) [MP0262];
new_str: - 2024: fewer than one lakh went in the whole year, a fall of more than two lakh on 2023, after the market closed in June (BMET data, Prothom Alo) [MP0262];
problem: The source says fewer than one lakh went in all of 2024, not after the closure; as written it says up to a lakh went after Malaysia shut, contradicting the closure.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: - Malaysia issued visas to the end, some on 30 May, Ruhul Amin said at a 4 June briefing held on behalf of the panel of 101 agencies;
new_str: - Malaysia issued visas to the end, some on 30 May, Ruhul Amin, alias Swapan, a former BAIRA secretary general whom the article calls a businessman at the centre of the Malaysia syndicate, said at a 4 June briefing held on behalf of the panel of 101 agencies;
problem: The 'Ruhul Amin' at the agencies' 4 June 2024 briefing is the businessman Ruhul Amin alias Swapan (the source's line 31), not the expatriates' welfare secretary Md Ruhul Amin named a few items later; the bare name merges the two people.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: the state minister said more or less all of the 100 approved agencies were responsible, held the stranded workers' papers, and that those workers would go first when the market reopened [MP0123, MP0124, MP0127, MP0128, MP0129].
new_str: the state minister said more or less all of the 100 approved agencies were responsible and that those workers would go first when the market reopened, and Prothom Alo reported that more or less all 100 agencies held the stranded workers' papers [MP0123, MP0124, MP0127, MP0128, MP0129].
problem: Attribution: that the agencies held the workers' papers is Prothom Alo's own reporting (MP0127), not the state minister's statement.

section: Is it open now, and who can go?
old_str: - **Agencies:** Malaysia allowed 337 Bangladeshi agencies to work, BOESL (Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Ltd, the government-owned recruiting agency) and the 25 processing agencies among them; under the MoU (memorandum of understanding) of 18 December 2022, choosing and listing the agencies is the job of Malaysia's human resources ministry (see The processing agency: the toll gate; see Who controls it) [MP0441, MP0438].
new_str: - **Agencies:** Malaysia agreed to list 338 Bangladeshi agencies: BOESL (Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Ltd, the government-owned recruiting agency), 25 processing agencies and 312 recruiting agencies; under the Bangladesh-Malaysia MoU (memorandum of understanding), choosing and listing the agencies is the job of Malaysia's human resources ministry (see The processing agency: the toll gate; see Who controls it) [Z0144, MP0438].
problem: States as fact the 337 from a newspaper summary (MP0441) where the Ministry's own announcement (Z0144) gives 338 (1 + 25 + 312), as the guide itself does under The processing agency; prefer the official figure (the 337/338 Need to know can stay). The MoU date '18 December 2022' contradicts BMET's office order dating the MoU to 19 December 2021 (W0027) and the guide's 'the 2021 MoU' elsewhere; leave the date to the Need to know.

section: How a job reaches you, and who takes a cut
old_str: and that under the MoU valid until December 2026 Malaysia would set the final number of Bangladeshi agencies on its own vetting, from the list of 423 [MP0381, MP0414, MP0415].
new_str: and that under the MoU valid until December 2026 Malaysia would set the final number of Bangladeshi agencies on its own vetting, from the list of 423 [MP0414, MP0415].
problem: MP0381 is about something else (the 22 June 2026 talks on regularising or returning irregular and jailed Bangladeshis), not Mahdi Amin's 30 July 2026 statement.

section: What you pay, and what you earn and keep
old_str: No cap is set for 2026 private-agency recruitment: the agencies proposed at most Tk 2.5 to 3 lakh, the figure the minister expects, and the state minister says nobody followed the old cap [YD0007, YA0066, G0012].
new_str: Until mid-November 2026 no cap was set for 2026 private-agency recruitment: on 5 November the agencies proposed at most Tk 2.5 to 3 lakh and the minister said the private-agency cost could fall in that range, and in October the state minister said nobody had followed the old cap [YD0007, YA0066, G0012].
problem: 2026 status contradiction: says in the present tense that no cap is set, though the next sentence (MP0459, 15 November 2026) says the cost has been fixed at Tk 1,54,000 and the section lead says the same. Also 'the figure the minister expects' overstates YA0066, where he said the cost 'could be' Tk 2.5 to 3 lakh.

old_str: - **Know what you should pay.** No cap is set for 2026, and the old one was not followed (see The cap; What people really pay) [YD0007, G0012].
new_str: - **Know what you should pay.** On 15 November 2026 the minister told parliament the cost of sending a worker had been fixed at Tk 1,54,000; which notice sets it, and whether it binds private agencies, is not yet published (see The cap; What people really pay) [MP0459]. The old cap was not followed [G0012].
problem: 2026 status contradiction: still says no cap is set for 2026, which the newer cited fact in The cap and Status (MP0459, 15 November 2026: cost fixed at Tk 1,54,000) contradicts.

section: Work visa: company worker (PLKS) (outside Background; 2026 status consistency)
old_str: Closed to new workers since 31 May 2024; where the restart stands, and what not to do until the Ministry issues instructions, is in Background ([Is it open now, and who can go?](#is-it-open-now-and-who-can-go)) [U0042].
new_str: Closed to new workers from 31 May 2024 and reopening since October 2026; where the restart stands is in Background ([Is it open now, and who can go?](#is-it-open-now-and-who-can-go)) [U0042, Z0151, MP0465].
problem: 2026 status contradiction: the opening still reads as if the corridor were simply closed and the Ministry's instructions not yet issued, while Status now says recruitment restarted on 15 October and medical tests began by 19 November under the Ministry's 28 October instructions (Z0151, MP0465).

section: How a job reaches you, and who takes a cut
old_str: A Malaysian committee chose the 25 without the Bangladesh government, 17 of them had never sent a worker to Malaysia, and Prothom Alo reported allegations that Amin and Swapan again decided who joined [A0029, A0027, YB0028].
new_str: A Malaysian committee chose the 25 with no involvement of the Bangladesh government, the Ministry said; 17 of them had never sent a worker to Malaysia, by Prothom Alo's analysis of BMET data; and Prothom Alo reported allegations that Amin and Swapan again decided who joined [A0029, A0027, YB0028].
problem: Drops attribution: that the Bangladesh government had no part is the Ministry's own statement (A0029), and the 17 is Prothom Alo's analysis (A0027); as written both read as established fact.
